statement: For nearest-neighbor FPP on Z^d, d>=2, with every edge weight in [a,b], 0<a<b, the n-edge axial path is uniquely minimizing whenever n(b-a)<2a. In the iid nondegenerate case its passage-time variance is exactly n Var(tau), and transverse displacement is zero.
assumptions: iid and positive variance only for the variance conclusion
proof_or_counterexample: Every nonaxial path has at least n+2 edges and cost >=(n+2)a>nb; the axial path has cost <=nb. Its iid edge sum has variance n Var(tau).
remaining_gap: Independent review; this is a finite-scale special case and does not supply asymptotic KPZ exponents.

statement: For any fixed M>=2 and rho<1, no law-independent integer N makes Var T(0,Mn e1)<=rho M Var T(0,n e1) hold for all n>=N and every nondegenerate continuous iid weight law supported in [1,2].
proof_or_counterexample: Given N choose n>=max(1,N), then 0<epsilon<min(1,2/(Mn)). L1 makes both times sums of iid Uniform weights; their variance ratio Var(T_Mn)/(M Var(T_n)) equals 1 exactly, violating the claimed strict contraction.
remaining_gap: Does not obstruct a law-dependent N(F); establish exponents for one fixed law to approach P0110.

statement: For a fixed epsilon>0, iid Uniform[1,1+epsilon] undirected nearest-neighbor FPP on Z^d, d>=2, has the axial n-edge path uniquely minimizing almost surely if and only if n epsilon<=2. In that range Var T(0,n e1)=n epsilon^2/12. Above it a cheaper parallel detour has probability at least ((n epsilon-2)/((4n+4)epsilon))^(2n+2)>0.
proof_or_counterexample: Use L1 below equality and the almost-sure strict axial upper-endpoint bound at equality. Above equality choose delta=(n epsilon-2)/(4n+4); condition the n axial edges within delta of the upper endpoint and the n+2 edge-disjoint detour edges within delta of the lower endpoint. The detour saves at least (n epsilon-2)/2 and the 2n+2 independent edge intervals have the displayed probability.
remaining_gap: Independent review and all fixed-law large-scale exponent matching; the result classifies certainty of a finite axial geodesic, not asymptotic wandering.
